cap: Thyroid cancers sorted by cell of origin. Follicular cells give papillary carcinoma (Orphan Annie nuclei, psammoma bodies, lymph spread), follicular carcinoma (capsular or vascular invasion, blood spread) and anaplastic carcinoma (TP53 loss); C cells give medullary carcinoma with calcitonin and amyloid; B cells give lymphoma in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
teach: Ask first which cell the tumor came from. Follicular-cell cancers make thyroglobulin and, when differentiated, take up radioiodine; the C-cell cancer makes calcitonin, ignores radioiodine and is inherited in MEN2A and MEN2B. The markers in the bottom band follow directly from the cell of origin.
